name: Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan (Taliban)

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024: land area 652,230 km2 (World Bank AG.LND.TOTL.K2); high adds ~3% for inland water.

population.note: asOf 2025: 43,844,111 (World Bank). Range allows for 2026 change.

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 2026 p.240 (as quoted on the Afghan Armed Forces article): 150,000, down from 165,000-170,000 in 2022-23 (75,000 full-time + 90,000 local militia, IISS 2022). The personnel list still shows IISS 2025: 172,000. Taliban claim 190,000 under the Ministry of Defense (CIA Factbook 2025) = high. World Bank 165,000 (2020) refers to the former republic.

trainedReserves.note: IISS: no formal reserve. Mid/high are educated allowances for callable local militias (IISS 2022 counted 90,000 local militia).

supportPersonnel.note: Active 150,000 minus infantry P roles 120,000 = 30,000. Small air arm, border and logistics units, staff; Taliban forces are mostly infantry.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Insurgent-style mobilisation of tribal/religious networks; 2% is ~0.9 million men, comparable to total Taliban mobilisation claims; equipment and pay are the limits.

count.note: Educated guess. Taliban 'regular' formations (corps such as 205 Al-Badr, Badri 313 battalion) operating as organised infantry. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghan_Armed_Forces)

quality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: captured M4/M16, HMMWVs; few heavy weapons.

training.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: Badri 313 and similar 'regular' units trained since 2021.

count.note: Educated guess. Bulk of the Islamic Emirate Army: dispersed light infantry/irregulars. Ministry of Interior forces (Taliban claim 215,000) excluded. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghan_Armed_Forces)

training.note: Rubric 0.5: battle-hardened insurgent veterans, decentralised, irregular.

count.note: List: T-55 110+ and T-62M 100 (IISS 2024 as quoted) = 210 on paper (high); serviceable number is an educated guess (mid 60, low 20) - few seen beyond parades and the 2025 border clashes.
List: BMP-1 350, BMP-2 150, BTR-70 360, BTR-50 100, M113A2 173, M1117 636 (IISS 2024), MaxxPro 70 = ~1,840 on paper; serviceable share is an educated guess.
List: M-30 232, D-30 41 (IISS 2024), BM-21 3 = 276 on paper (high); serviceable share an educated guess.

Educated guess. Ex-Afghan Air Force Mi-17, UH-60 and MD-530 left in 2021 and flown in small numbers; many flown to Uzbekistan in 2021 or disabled. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghan_Armed_Forces)

quality.note: Rubric 0.25: ex-ANA Mi-17/UH-60/MD-530 without OEM support.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: decentralised, patrimonial command (Giustozzi 2016 as cited on the article); effective at insurgent warfare, untested at combined arms.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.5: strong ideological and network cohesion, but loose, factional (Haqqani vs Kandahari) structure.

morale.note: Rubric 0.75-1.0: ideologically motivated victors of 2021; fanatical in home defence; lower for conventional offensives (2025-26 border clashes with Pakistan).

weapons.note: Anchor 8: captured US small arms, night vision and vehicles; no precision fires.

armor.note: Anchor 7-8: few T-55/T-62; mostly unarmoured technicals and HMMWVs.

ships.note: Landlocked; no naval forces (not absent-in-era, simply none).

fortification.note: Anchor 7: field fortifications, cave/tunnel complexes; former US/ANA bases.

logistics.note: Anchor 7: pickup trucks, captured trucks, porters; very limited sustainment.

communications.note: Anchor 8: radios, mobile phones, commercial internet.

isr.note: Anchor 7: no aircraft-based ISR beyond a few helicopters and commercial drones.

air.note: Anchor 8-9: Taliban air arm per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghan_Air_Force: Mi-8/17 7, UH-60 7, Mi-24 4, MD 530F 5, Cessna 208 6, An-26/32 3, A-29 1, L-39 1 (34 listed, airworthiness uncertain). 1970s-80s airframes (anchor 9 era) flown without radar, data links or precision weapons, so below 9; not below 8 since all are post-1943 types. Audit follow-up 2026-10-29: 6.0 -> 8.3, 6.0 sat below anchor 7, where powered military aviation starts; re-rated from the helicopters and light aircraft it flies.

cyber.note: Anchor 9 (1990 networks) is the lowest level at which the category exists: the state runs on mobile and commercial internet networks; no documented state cyber force, so no credit toward 10. Audit follow-up 2026-10-29: 5.0 -> 9.0, 5.0 sat below anchor 9, the first cyber level; set at the floor.

gdpPerCapita.note: asOf 2024. GDP (2011 int$) 67,065,060,104 / population 43,844,111 = 1,530. Range +/-15%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

gdp.note: asOf 2024. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 83,778,963,278 x 0.8005 (US GDP deflator 2011/2021) = 67,065,060,104 2011 int$. Range +/-15% for PPP benchmark uncertainty and the relative-price drift the rebase ignores. https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/AFG/indicator/NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD?format=json Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank: 1.83% in 2021 (last republic year); Factbook 3.3% (2019). Taliban-era spending unpublished; range is an educated band.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2024: industry incl. construction 14.5% of GDP (World Bank).

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Chronic food deficit; dependent on aid and imports after the 2021 aid cut-off.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 22,142,579 x share of males aged 15-19 11.274% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 499,278. Male population from SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN. Males only (conscript-pool convention); about double if women are counted. Range +/-10% for single-year cohort variation.

roadKm.note: asOf 2021: 34,903 km total, 17,903 km paved (mid) (list as quoted).

railKm.note: Educated guess. No World Bank or Factbook rail figure. Known lines: Hairatan-Mazar (75 km), Khaf-Herat (Afghan section ~60 km), Turkmen lines at Torghundi/Aqina (~50 km). (context page: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/factbook/factbook.json/master/south-asia/af.json)

majorPorts.note: Landlocked; CIA Factbook lists no ports. Imports via Karachi, Bandar Abbas/Chabahar and Central Asian rail.

merchantTonnage.note: Landlocked; no merchant marine listed by the CIA Factbook.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Light infantry living off the land and local networks; no vehicle-based sustainment for distant operations.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Donkeys, horses, camels widely used in rural transport (not from FAO data).

nuclearWarheads.note: FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces 2026 lists nine nuclear-armed states; Afghanistan is not one of them.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.3: the rubric's own example - mountains, harsh climate, deep strategic depth, population support for resistance to invaders.

notes: Modern snapshot asOf 2025-26. The armed forces are the Taliban's 'Islamic Emirate Army' since August 2021: a former insurgency organised into nominal corps, with captured US/ANA equipment (much unserviceable). Doctrine archetype-insurgent: they would fight any invader as dispersed light infantry. Conventional counts from the Wikipedia equipment list (IISS 2024 as quoted) are paper holdings; serviceable mids are educated guesses (grade D). Population inside ne:AFG (World Bank 2025). Money via derived:ppp-rebase-2011 (World Bank GDP 2024). Border clashes with Pakistan in October 2025 and February-March 2026 (Pakistani airstrikes on Kandahar, Bagram, Paktika). Ministry of Interior forces excluded. The Taliban government is recognised only by Russia (2025).
